title: W3 VERIFY (text against source): state.json structures read against their codified ratios
description: Wave 3's text-against-source audit, with the failure mode this wave carries: a record that restates a configured constant as though a decision with reasoning had produced it, or that quietly widens a gate list, a bound or a cost rule while claiming to codify it. The source here is a JSON file, so the audit is exact - the record's ratio and the structure's actual content can be put side by side with no interpretation at all. You audit the canonical id set T-390 forwarded. Rotation (F6): identity distinct from every prior verifier and producer.
acceptance_criteria: INPUT IS T-390's CANONICAL LIST - quote it.

TEXT-AGAINST-SOURCE, SIDE BY SIDE, AGAINST THE LIVE JSON: for every record, print the state.json structure it codifies (by key path) and its ratio next to each other, and state ENACTS / NARROWS / WIDENS / DRIFTS. All four human_gates items present and unreworded; all six limits values correct as of publication; every cost_policy rule the record claims to codify quoted accurately; protected_paths entries exact. A single silently dropped gate item is a REJECT.

FACT-VERSUS-RATIO TEST: for each record ask whether it codifies a NORM or merely restates a number. A ratio that says nothing an agent could act on beyond the value itself is a REJECT under the D1 distinction the ledger applied.

THE BELOW-BAND HONESTY CHECK: run python3 .harness/bin/token_share.py yourself and confirm the frontier-budget record's dicta carries a measured number with its date, and that the record states the band's operator-heuristic provenance rather than implying a literature-derived threshold. A record that presents the band as established fact is a REJECT.

CROSS-WAVE SUBSUMPTION HELD: confirm no wave-3 record re-promulgates a wave-1 norm (P-024, P-030, P-020, P-029 in particular). A duplicate at the doctrine level is the failure PR-032 exists to record.

NO STALE LINE ANCHOR SHIPPED: no record may cite state.json by line number; every path:lines token in sources or validity must be opened and confirmed to contain the cited content (path:lines resolves on file existence alone, so nothing else catches this).
CD3 grep for P-023 and 'backfill'; CD5 check against the NOT-CODIFIED column; CD8 every home cited with the primary named.
SHOW AND CITE for every record on the canonical list, exit codes pasted.

TEST FLOOR: python3 -m unittest discover -s .harness/tests -p "test_precedent*.py" prints a 'Ran N tests' line with N >= 252 and OK (252 measured live 2026-08-13 by the planner; if N is higher, name T-376 as the landed repair rather than absorbing the delta) (your own Ran N line).

VERDICT: P-022 self-done available; record your identity and confirm you are none of the prior verifiers or producers. LEAK AND STYLE HYGIENE (the board and .harness/tasks/*.json are tracked): no absolute filesystem path, no username and no emoji in any note or artifact you write. Temp-root replays print absolute paths - redact them to a placeholder before pasting. Two prior tasks leaked an operator home path exactly this way.

PR-049 is the closest call, because a band is a number; it survives because the ratio also carries the measurement instrument, the breach consequence and the delegation duty, none of which is derivable from 53-65 alone. RECORDED FINDINGS (defects in published records; remedy is a voiding act, coordinator-owned, not applied by me):

F1 (PR-049, most substantive). PR-049 declares cost_policy.rules[1] SUBSUMED, but its ratio carries only the short contract-prose form of that rule. The live rule names four things the coordinator produces (decisions, dispatch prompts, join syntheses, and short reports) and four things that are dispatched to the cheap tier (document drafting, bulk analysis, corpus digestion, and long-form synthesis). The ratio carries three and two respectively: "short reports" drops from the produce side, and "corpus digestion" and "long-form synthesis" drop from the delegate side. Because the ratio is the only operative text and rule 2 is declared subsumed, a coordinator reading the registry alone would not learn that corpus digestion and long-form synthesis must be delegated. This is a NARROWING of a duty, and it is not disclosed -- the dicta says only "storage homes ... are subsumed by this record". Mitigation on the record's side, stated for fairness: the sentence it does carry reproduces its contract-prose home verbatim, and under CD1 the prose home is canonical, so the record is faithful to the canonical text and the divergence is really between the two homes. Not a criterion-named REJECT; forwarded for the join.

F2 (PR-049, citation scope). The delegation sentence the ratio carries lives at contract-document line 158, which is OUTSIDE PR-049's cited range 136-148 and INSIDE the block 149-161 that PR-050 declares as its own primary home. Proven mechanically: extracting lines 136 through 148 and counting the sentence returns 0; grepping the whole file for it returns line 158 only. The token resolves on file existence and range validity, so neither cite nor conflicts nor stale can see this -- it is exactly the class this criterion exists to catch, in its "confirmed to contain the cited content" half. The range does fully contain the frontier-budget norm that is PR-049's principal ratio, so the anchor is mis-scoped rather than wrong.

F3 (PR-050, disclosed narrowing understated). PR-050 declares rule 7 subsumed. The live rule lists four high-verifiability execution categories (code with tests, audits with replayable evidence, corpus reading with page-cited claims, and research) and names four roles it assigns to the cheap tier (workers, verifiers, evolution-analyst, research-librarian). The ratio carries three categories and no roles: "research" drops, as do all four role names. The record does disclose that the state.json text is fuller -- "the fullest single statement lives at state.json cost_policy.rules entry 7" -- but names only "the haiku evidence citation" as the delta, which understates its extent. As with F1 the ratio reproduces its declared CD1 primary (contract line 155) verbatim, and the governing test it does carry (verifiability) covers research on its own terms, so the operative loss is small. Recorded, not a REJECT.

F4 (PR-047, added clause, no defect). The ratio appends "and do not brief-replay a change that can break the control plane", a clause present in neither home. It is the contrapositive of the source's own "control-plane/contract tasks get full adversarial replay" and therefore adds no obligation beyond the source. Recorded for completeness because an added clause is the shape a widening takes; verified here to be a restatement.

F5 (PR-049, dating). The below-band measurements in the dicta (33.8 / 42.0 and 35.1 / 43.5) are dated by task anchor rather than by calendar date. The anchor resolves -- T-375's notes are timestamped 2026-08-12 -- so the dating is recoverable, but the record does not print it. The two wave-3 siblings do print a calendar date on their readings, which is the better pattern. Recorded as a below-band-honesty observation, explicitly NOT a REJECT: the criterion's REJECT trigger is presenting the band as established fact, and PR-049 does the opposite in unusually direct language.

F6 (five records, CD8 wording, and one home-selection inconsistency). PR-041, PR-046, PR-047, PR-048 and PR-049 use "storage home X is subsumed by this record (CD8)" without naming a primary in the word CD8 uses; the primary is identifiable in each case from the ledger and the ratio text, so this is a wording delta rather than a substantive failure. Separately and more interestingly: PR-046's ratio follows the NARROWER state.json wording ("harness-verifier defaults to sonnet") rather than its own declared prose primary at line 130 ("Reviewer tier defaults to sonnet"), while PR-049 and PR-050 do the reverse, following prose over the fuller state.json. Same producer, same wave, opposite home-selection rule. PR-046's choice is honest on its own terms because its declared_width is narrow and its scope condition is coordinator-dispatch-scoped, but the inconsistency is the thing worth forwarding: the epic has no stated rule for which home governs the ratio when the two homes differ in reach, and F1, F3 and F6 are all instances of that single missing rule.

OPEN-QUESTION: which home governs the RATIO TEXT when a norm's prose home and its state.json home differ in reach? CD1 fixes canonicity (prose is canonical) and CD8 fixes citation (one record, all homes, primary named), but neither says whether a record that declares a state.json structure SUBSUMED must carry that structure's full content or may carry only the canonical prose short form. F1, F3 and F6 are three independent instances. This is not mine to close; it is forwarded to the join alongside the six OPEN-QUESTIONs T-390 forwarded, all of which still stand.
